personalizedFeedback.title: REDUCING FACIAL FAT
personalizedFeedback.description:
Your bone structure is actually quite balanced on paper, but it is currently *hidden under a layer of soft tissue*. The puffiness in your cheeks and the lack of a defined jawline are the primary factors keeping your frontal score in the 50s.
To fix this, you need to reach a *lower body fat percentage* (ideally 12-15%). This will "unmask" your underlying bone structure, sharpen your gonial angle, and create the hollows needed for a more masculine, elite read.

personalizedFeedback.title: CORRECTING PROFILE CONVEXITY
personalizedFeedback.description:
Your side profile is your weakest area due to *skeletal recession*. The combination of a recessed maxilla and a recessed chin creates a convex curve that makes the face look weaker and the nose look larger than it actually is.
The most effective physical fix for the chin is a *sliding genioplasty*, which moves the chin bone forward. For the maxilla, a *maxillary advancement* (surgical) would be the gold standard to create a more vertical, harmonious profile.

personalizedFeedback.title: NASAL REFINEMENT
personalizedFeedback.description:
The *dorsal hump* and the acute nasolabial angle contribute to the "heavy" look of your midface. Because your chin is recessed, the nose becomes the most prominent feature of your profile, which creates a visual imbalance.
A *rhinoplasty* to remove the hump and slightly rotate the tip upward would improve the nasolabial angle and reduce the perceived convexity of the face.

personalizedFeedback.title: SKIN QUALITY OPTIMIZATION
personalizedFeedback.description:
There is noticeable *texture and congestion* on the lower third of your face, specifically around the chin. This detracts from the overall cleanliness of your look and draws attention to the recessed area of the jaw.
A strict *dermatological routine* involving salicylic acid or retinoids, combined with professional extractions, is required to clear the skin and improve the light-reflecting quality of your face.

personalizedFeedback.title: EYE AREA COMPACTNESS
personalizedFeedback.description:
You have good eye spacing, but *moderate upper eyelid exposure* makes the eyes look slightly tired or less "intense." This is often a result of the orbital rim position and soft tissue distribution.
While surgery (blepharoplasty) is an option, *reducing overall systemic inflammation* and lowering facial fat can sometimes improve the appearance of the orbital area by reducing puffiness and tightening the surrounding skin.
